findings.title: Pause action not rendered for Grafana rules in list view
findings.body: The Pause menu item is gated by `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, which is false when `rulerRule` is undefined. After this PR the list view no longer passes a `rulerRule` for Grafana rules, so even though `canPause` (computed from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) is correctly true with proper permissions, the user cannot pause/resume Grafana rules from the list view. Either keep fetching the rulerRule just for this action, refetch it on click, or render the menu item with a GrafanaPromRuleDTO-aware pause component.

findings.title: Delete action not rendered for Grafana rules in list view
findings.body: The Delete menu item is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule && (...)`. With the list view no longer providing `rulerRule` for Grafana rules, `rulerRule` is undefined, so Delete is not rendered even though the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` check correctly reports `canDelete = true`. Users will lose the ability to delete Grafana rules from the list view. The component or its handler needs to support a path that does not require a `RulerRuleDTO`.

findings.title: Silence drawer never opens for Grafana rules in list view
findings.body: `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is only mounted when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, which is false when `rule` is undefined. In the new list view flow, `rule` is no longer passed to `RuleActionsButtons` (only `promRule`), so the Silence menu item appears in the dropdown (because `canSilence` is computed from `promRule`) but clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer = true` and the drawer never mounts, silently doing nothing. Either gate the menu item on the same condition, or refactor the drawer to accept a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`.

findings.title: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterView switch
findings.body: The previous code rendered `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ...>` for the `grafana` case inside the `rules.map(...)`. After this change the new `<GrafanaRuleListItem ...>` is missing the `key` prop, while the sibling branches (`case 'datasource'` and the `default` case) still pass `key={key}`. Without a key on one branch React will fall back to array indices, which can cause incorrect component reuse, lost local state, and unnecessary remounts when the list is filtered, paginated or re-ordered.

findings.title: Federated rule groups no longer detected as immutable
findings.body: `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` now hard-codes `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO to re-add support. The previous implementation derived this from `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. Because this hook is still used for non-Grafana (cloud/Mimir) rules via `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`, federated rule groups will no longer be considered `immutableRule`, meaning Update/Delete/Pause/Restore abilities may report `supported=true` for rules that should be read-only at the federation level. Re-introduce the federated check or document that this is an intentional regression.

findings.title: Removing Creating/Deleting state indicators is not covered by tests or docs
findings.body: The old `GrafanaGroupLoader` rendered `RuleOperation.Creating` items for rules present in the Ruler but not yet in Prometheus, and `RuleOperation.Deleting` items for rules only in Prometheus (with a `logWarning`). Both the implementation and the corresponding tests (`should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists`, `should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists`) have been removed. This is a user-visible UX regression (rules appear to vanish / reappear) but the change is not described in the PR description, nor in a changelog entry, and there is no test asserting the new behavior. Please document the intentional behavior change and add coverage.

findings.title: Test asserting exactly 4 menu items encodes the missing Pause/Delete regression
findings.body: The new test `should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked` asserts `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` after granting all of `AlertingRuleUpdate`, `AlertingRuleDelete`, `AlertingRuleCreate`, etc. With those permissions the abilities hooks report `canPause = true` and `canDelete = true`, but the menu items for Pause and Delete are not rendered because of the `rulerRule`/`rule` gates in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` (lines 123 and 165) and `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` (line 104). The test currently passes because the bug is hard-coded into the expected count; once the Pause/Delete render bug is fixed, this test will fail unless updated.

findings.title: Stale `// duplicate` comment
findings.body: Inside `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` the line `const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate` carries a trailing `// duplicate` comment that does not explain anything (it doesn't say what is duplicated or why). It looks like a leftover TODO that should be removed or replaced with a meaningful comment.

findings.title: Misleading `@deprecated` on `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` is marked `@deprecated Use {@link useAllRulerRuleAbilities} instead`, but `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` is not a drop-in replacement: it has a different signature (`RulerRuleDTO | undefined` + `RuleGroupIdentifierV2` vs. `CombinedRule`). The wrapper itself (and `useAlertRuleAbility` / `useAlertRuleAbilities`) still calls `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`, so this deprecation is contradictory and will be confusing to readers. Either remove the deprecation, update the message, or finish migrating the `useAlertRuleAbility*` hooks.

findings.title: `RuleActionsButtons` silently renders null for invalid props
findings.body: `getEditableIdentifier` returns `undefined` and the component returns `null` whenever neither a `RulerRuleDTO` nor a Grafana `promRule` is supplied. Previously the prop `rule: RulerRuleDTO` was required and an identifier was always produced. The new permissive typing means a caller can pass `{}` (no rulerRule, no grafana promRule) and get an empty cell in the row instead of an obvious error. The TypeScript `RequireAtLeastOne` only narrows at the callsite, not at the place that actually uses both fields. At minimum, callers should be warned explicitly (a `logWarning` is logged but it does not propagate to the UI), and ideally a runtime error would be raised in development.

findings.title: `useRulerRuleAbilities(undefined, ...)` still calls `useIsRuleEditable` from the list view
findings.body: Even though `GrafanaRuleListItem` no longer provides a `rulerRule`, `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` and `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` both still invoke `useRulerRuleAbility(s)` / `useRulerRuleAbilities` for every row, which in turn call `useIsRuleEditable(rulesSourceName, rule)` internally. If `useIsRuleEditable` issues a Ruler network call (as its name suggests), the goal of this PR — eliminating Ruler traffic from the alert list view — is not actually achieved for Grafana rules. Verify the implementation of `useIsRuleEditable` and short-circuit the hook when no `rulerRule` is provided (e.g., reuse the same `skipToken` pattern used for `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`).
